name: MutableString concurrent publication preserves complete Unicode

input.source_text: module M { public fun run() -> Object { let text = m"éè"; NativeFixture.concurrently_replace(text, "üöä"); [text.to_string(), text.length] } } M.run()

applicability.reason: Supported. C060 leaves MutableString not logically thread-safe but requires it to stay memory-safe, never expose invalid Unicode, and publish either old complete content or new complete content to a correctly synchronized observer. The recorded blocker was structural rather than semantic: runtime values were `Rc<RefCell<..>>`, which is not `Send`, so no value could reach a second thread and the clause was unobservable by construction. The shared cells are now `Arc<Mutex<..>>`, so the write happens on a REAL second thread that is joined before the read, which is what makes the observer correctly synchronized in C060's sense. Multi-byte content on both sides makes the Unicode half observable: a torn write would leave a partial scalar, so round-tripping the exact text AND its scalar length is the evidence.
